config.title: 1g. EHR baselines on real data: PIMA Indians Diabetes, four hospitals
config.description: Fixed before any run (10 November 2026); nothing below was changed after seeing a result. Real records: the PIMA Indians Diabetes Database (768 women of Pima heritage, 8 numeric features, diabetes within five years yes / no), split across the 4 hospitals with a Dirichlet label split (alpha = 1.0) drawn once with partition_seed. Each hospital holds out 25% of its records; held-out records are used only for the final scores, never for training, early stopping or choosing settings. Every setting is a default: the platform's TabNet and training settings for EHR (as in 1b), scikit-learn defaults for the forests and boosting. Zero values in glucose, blood pressure, skin fold, insulin and BMI are physiologically impossible and are treated as missing, as is usual for this dataset (the file itself codes them as 0); each hospital fills them by KNN imputation (k = 5) fitted on its own training split, and standardises with its own training-split mean and SD (nothing shared). The centralised model does the same on the union of the training splits. Scores are computed on the held-out records of all hospitals pooled (positive = diabetes); F1 and recall use the 0.5 threshold. 3 seeds (model initialisation, data order, forest / boosting random state); the partition is the same in every seed.

preprocessing.scaling: each hospital's training-split mean and SD

tabnet.settings: platform TabNet: n_d = n_a = 16, 3 steps, gamma 1.3, ghost batch 64, sparsity weight 1e-3

logistic_regression.settings: one linear layer, softmax cross-entropy, no weight decay

gradient_boosting.settings: GradientBoostingClassifier defaults (100 stages, depth 3, learning rate 0.1)
